entries.what_happened: Two manuscripts. (1) 'The p-adic section conjecture' (OpenAI, 6 October 2026) claims the local p-adic section conjecture: for every prime p, every finite extension k/ℚ_p and every smooth proper geometrically connected curve X/k of genus at least two, the map from X(k) to the set of continuous group-homomorphic splittings s: G_k → π_1(X) of π_1(X) → G_k, modulo conjugation by the geometric fundamental group π_1(X_k̄), is bijective (Theorem 1.1, thm:section). Surjectivity (Section 7) is argued as follows. A completion theorem (Theorem thm:completion, proved in Section 6 from patching in Section 3, collar roots in Sections 4 and 5, and cited inputs from Mochizuki–Tsujimura, Amini–Baker–Brugallé–Rabinoff and Raynaud / Bosch–Lütkebohmert) places the separable closure of k(X) inside the completion of the universal étale function field. Rank-one localisations of a section are excluded by Koenigsmann's birational section theorem and an explicit two-valuation argument (Lemma no-rank-one-section). In the remaining case the closed point has residue field k, because the section surjects onto G_k, and Pop–Stix's type-2h analysis then identifies the section with a point section. Injectivity (end of Section 7) is a Kummer-type argument on the Jacobian, using the local logarithm. The same manuscript also states a global theorem over number fields K: for a smooth proper geometrically connected C/K of genus at least two, C(K) → Sec(C/K) is bijective whenever the finite-cover descent locus equals C(K) (Theorem global-descent). It gives three corollaries under which that equality holds: abelian targets (Corollary global-abelian-target), an elliptic target E/ℚ with Selmer corank zero at one prime (Corollary global-selmer-target), and the modular curves X_0(N) and X_1(N) of genus at least two over ℚ (Corollary global-modular-curves). (2) 'Étale covers with a prescribed exterior sheet' (OpenAI, 24 September 2026) does not bear on sections. Over k̄, for a smooth proper hyperbolic curve X and finitely many disjoint disks V_i with exterior U, it constructs a connected smooth proper Y and a finite étale surjective g: Y → X such that a component of g^{-1}(U) maps isomorphically to U and every component of g^{-1}(V_i) has degree divisible by p over V_i. It mentions no sections, rational points or Galois splittings, and the p-adic manuscript does not cite it.
entries.delivers: Local case: for k finite over ℚ_p and genus at least two, both halves of the bijection (surjectivity and injectivity) for the full arithmetic π_1 with conjugacy by the geometric π_1, which is what the list's (a) and (b) describe. This is not the frozen quantifier: a finite extension of ℚ_p is not a finitely generated field, so the local theorem does not by itself settle the problem as frozen. Global case: for a smooth proper geometrically connected C/K of genus at least two over a number field K, κ_C is bijective under the finite-cover descent equality. The manuscript supplies that equality only for the listed cases: X_0(N) and X_1(N) of genus at least two over ℚ (the abstract says 'this includes' these); abelian targets with A(K) finite and Sha(A/K)_div = 0, or a Jacobian with J(K) finite and Sha(J/K)_div = 0; and curves with a nonconstant ℚ-morphism to an elliptic curve E with s_p(E) = 0 for at least one p. The manuscript does not claim to settle the section conjecture in general. Against the list: the splitting-and-conjugacy formulation and the bijectivity match (a) and (b) on the covered curves. The quantifiers differ. The list names no genus and all finitely generated fields; the paper assumes genus at least two and characteristic zero, treats finite extensions of ℚ_p locally, and treats only number fields globally.
entries.remains: If the claim is correct, the frozen problem stays open in general. (i) Finitely generated fields other than number fields and finite extensions of ℚ_p: for example function fields of curves over number fields or finite fields, and fields of positive characteristic, since the manuscript works only in characteristic zero. (ii) For number fields, every curve whose finite-cover descent locus is not known to equal its rational points, including curves of genus at least two outside the three listed criteria. (iii) Curves of genus 0 and 1, which the genus-two hypothesis excludes (the frozen statement names no genus). (iv) Without the descent equality, the global bijection is not claimed; the manuscript says the equality 'remains a separate arithmetic hypothesis'.
entries.direction: proves the conjecture for finite extensions of ℚ_p (genus at least two), and proves it for listed number-field cases; no general proof
entries.conditional_on: Global results (Section 8, 'Global consequences via finite descent'): the finite-cover equality (eq. finite-cover-equality) is an assumed hypothesis. For the modular curves it is supplied by Stoll's Corollary 8.8 (Finite descent obstructions and rational points on curves), as corrected by Stoll's erratum. The abelian-target corollary uses Stoll's Corollary 8.1 and Theorem 8.6. The elliptic-target corollary uses the companion manuscript 'The Selmer converse for elliptic curves at every prime' (OpenAI, October 2026), cited as OpenAISelmerConverse2026, Theorem 1.1, which I did not read. The surjectivity argument uses Pop–Stix's valuative localisation (Theorem 26) and their type-2h analysis (Section 6.1), and Koenigsmann's Proposition 2.4(2); all three are cited as preprint versions. The completion theorem uses Mochizuki–Tsujimura's resolution theorem, Amini–Baker–Brugallé–Rabinoff's Theorem 7.7 and Raynaud / Bosch–Lütkebohmert uniformisation. The global corollaries also use Harari–Stix's Theorem 2.1 and Stix's finite-support corollary, and the real-place step uses Bresciani–Vistoli's real section theorem. The 'Étale covers' manuscript is not used by this one.
entries.doubts: (1) The last step of surjectivity is delegated. The text says 'Equivalently, the type-2h conclusion of [Pop–Stix, Section 6.1] gives s = s_a', and the sentence 'For the full étale tower the horizontal inertia is trivial, and the horizontal decomposition group is the point section at a' is asserted without argument. (2) 'The valuation transcendence inequality gives ratrank(Γ_w/Γ_k) ≤ 1' is stated with no reference and no proof. (3) Injectivity compresses its key step into one sentence: conjugate sections induce isomorphic G_k-actions on the geometric fibres of [n] on J, so fixed points are preserved. The text calls this 'the usual Kummer argument'. (4) The modular-curve corollary covers 'every positive integer N such that X_0(N) has genus at least two' without listing those N, and rests entirely on Stoll's Corollary 8.8. The text says the stated equalities are 'retained' under the erratum, so the claim depends on the erratum's corrected form of a published result, which the manuscript does not reprove. (5) Several cited inputs are 'preprint version' references (Pop–Stix, Koenigsmann, Harari–Stix, Betts–Stix). I did not check those versions. (6) The README notes a previous version of this manuscript (24 September 2026) with revised citations. I did not compare the versions.
